summary: Defines a conference event package for tightly coupled conferences using the SIP events framework, with the data format for notifications. Users can subscribe to a conference URI and are notified of changes such as who joined or left. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lets a program follow a conference call. The program asks the server running the call to keep it informed, and the server sends back a small XML document whenever somebody joins, leaves or changes state. Each document also carries a number, so that a subscriber can tell which update came first.

questions: who is in a sip conference
what is the sip conference event package
how to subscribe to a sip conference
subtitle: How a SIP client subscribes to a conference and is told who joined, who left and what changed.

tldr.problem: In a conference call, participants need to know who else is present and when that changes, and there was no standard way for a SIP client to be told.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a SIP event package called conference. A client subscribes to the conference URI, and the focus, which runs the conference, sends notifications carrying an XML document that describes the conference, its participants and their states.
tldr.outcome: The notifications normally carry only what changed, and each document carries a version number so a subscriber can put the pieces back together in the right order.

facts.label: Recommended notification rate
facts.value: No faster than once every 5 seconds

today: RFC 4575 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted. It registers the conference event package, the application/conference-info+xml media type, the XML namespace and the XML schema.

sections.title: What This Package Is For
sections.content:
The SIP events framework defines general mechanisms for subscribing to, and receiving notifications of, events within SIP networks. It introduces the notion of a package, which is a specific instantiation of that framework for a well-defined set of events. This RFC defines such a package for tightly coupled conferences, and it can be used by the conference notification service described in the SIP conferencing framework.

Subscriptions to a conference URI are routed to the focus that is handling the conference. The focus acts as the notifier and gives clients updates on the conference state. In SIP, a conference is represented by a URI, and that URI identifies a SIP user agent, called the focus, that is responsible for making sure every user in the conference can reach the others. The focus has the information needed to tell subscribers about the conference.

A participant in the conference may itself be another focus. To give a more complete participant list, the focus may subscribe to the conference package of the other focus to discover the participants of that cascaded conference, and can then include that information in its own notifications using the cascaded-focus element.

The information the package carries is the conference identifier or identifiers, the conference participants, optionally with their statuses and media descriptions, conference sidebars, and conference service URIs. The term roster is used throughout the document to refer collectively to the participants in a conference or a sub-conference.
sections.plainLanguage: A conference in SIP is handled by one server, the focus, which knows who is on the call. This RFC lets any client ask that focus to keep it posted about changes.

sections.title: How the Package Works
sections.content:
The name of the event package is conference, and it is carried in the Event and Allow-Events header fields.

This document does not define filters for the package. A SUBSCRIBE for a conference package sent without a body implies the default filtering policy: notifications are generated every time there is any change in the state of the conference, and notifications do not normally contain the full state but only the state that has changed. The exception is a NOTIFY sent in response to a SUBSCRIBE, which contains the full state of the information requested.

The default expiration time for a subscription to a conference is one hour. Once the conference ends, all subscriptions to it are terminated with a reason of noresource.

The body of a notification contains a conference information document, in the format listed in the Accept header field of the SUBSCRIBE or a package-specific default if that header was omitted. All subscribers and notifiers must support the application/conference-info+xml data format. If the Accept header is present it must include application/conference-info+xml and may include other types.

Because conference information contains very sensitive information, all subscriptions should be authenticated and then authorized before approval, with the authorization policy left to the administrator. It is recommended that all users in the conference be allowed to subscribe to the package.

The focus should generate notifications when a participant joins or leaves. Subject to local policy it may also report changes in participants' status, changes in their media types and other optional information. Changes in sidebar rosters should be reported to their participants and may be reported to others. Changes in conference identifiers and service URIs should be reported to the subscribers, and other changes in conference state may be reported.

Conferences are centralized, so SUBSCRIBE requests for a conference should not generally fork, and if forking happens in the network, subscribers to this package must not establish more than a single SIP dialog as a result of a single SUBSCRIBE request. For reasons of congestion control it is recommended that the server does not generate notifications for a single subscriber at a rate faster than once every 5 seconds. Conference state is ideally maintained in the element in which the conference resides, so the focus is the best-suited element to handle subscriptions, although cascaded foci may implement state agents.
sections.plainLanguage: A client subscribes to the conference's address and the server sends it an update whenever something changes. By default the update says only what changed, and the subscription lasts an hour unless the call ends first.

sections.title: The Conference Document
sections.content:
Conference information is an XML document that must be well-formed and valid, based on XML 1.0 and encoded using UTF-8. The namespace for the elements defined by this specification is the URN urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:conference-info.

The information is described by a hierarchical structure whose root element is conference-info. The root element is the only element that carries a meaningful version number for the whole document, and the version attribute must be included in it. The version is a 32-bit monotonically increasing integer scoped within a subscription. The server must increment it for each notification that reports a change in the conference document state, and for each partial notification it must be increased by one.

The root element has three attributes: entity, which holds the conference URI that an interested entity subscribes to; state, which says whether the document holds the whole conference information, only what has changed, or that the conference has ceased to exist; and version.

The root element is made up of conference-description, host-info, conference-state, users, sidebars-by-ref and sidebars-by-val child elements. A full conference document must at least include the conference-description and users child elements.

The conference-description describes the conference as a whole: display text, subject, a longer free text description and keywords that search engines can use, the URIs for reaching the conference with their purpose, such as participation or streaming, the URIs of auxiliary services such as a web page or a recording, a hint of how many users may be invited, and the media streams available to participants. The host-info element describes the entity hosting the conference. The conference-state element carries the number of users, whether the conference is active and whether it is locked, meaning that the roster cannot be added to although participants may leave.
sections.plainLanguage: The state of a conference is sent as an XML document with one root element and a handful of parts: a description of the conference, information about the host, the current state, and the list of users. Each document carries a version number so updates can be ordered.

sections.title: Partial Notifications and Coherent State
sections.content:
The package defines a basic partial notification mechanism using a state attribute, which every subscribing client must support. The elements of the document are divided into those that may be sent partially, because they carry a substantial amount of data that changes often, and those that are updated as whole pieces of data. The elements that may use the mechanism are conference-info, users, user, endpoint, sidebars-by-val and sidebars-by-ref, and future extensions to the schema must say which of their elements may use it too.

The state attribute says whether the information about the element is full, partial or deleted, and the default value is full. A child's state must be consistent with its parent's: if the parent is full, its children must be full; if the parent is partial, a child may be partial, full or deleted. A parent with deleted state should not contain child elements, and any information given for the children of a deleted parent must be ignored.

To make partial notifications work, the schema gives each element that may appear more than once under the same parent a key. The key is the set of mandatory attributes or sub-elements of the element, and its value must be unique among its siblings of the same type. The user element uses entity as its key, the endpoint element uses entity, the media element uses id, the entry element under sidebars-by-val uses entity, and sidebars-by-ref uses uri. Two keys of type xs:anyURI are equal when their UTF-8 representations are identical, so relative URIs and lexical white space are not recommended in keys.

The subscriber keeps a local version number for the whole document and a local copy of each element, with a table row for each key value of an element that has keys. The first time a NOTIFY with full state arrives, the subscriber sets its local version to the version in the document and populates its local data. Each later NOTIFY is compared with the local version: a document whose version is equal to or lower than the local one is discarded. A document with full or deleted state replaces the local information, and a deleted state for the whole conference means the conference has ceased to exist, so the subscriber should end the subscription by sending a SUBSCRIBE with Expires set to 0. For a partial document, if the version is more than one higher than the local version the subscriber must generate a subscription refresh to trigger a full state notification; if it is exactly one higher, the document is merged. When merging, an element with full state has its local content flushed and repopulated, an element with deleted state is removed, and an element with partial state is merged by looking up its key and applying the same rules to its children.
sections.plainLanguage: Updates usually mention only what changed, so a subscriber has to combine several documents to know the whole state. Every element has a key that identifies it, and every document has a version number, so the subscriber can tell which update is newer and can ask for a fresh full copy if an update arrives out of order.

sections.title: Participants, Endpoints and Media
sections.content:
The users element is a container of user elements, each describing one participant. A user has an entity attribute holding the participant's URI, which is a logical identifier corresponding to the authenticated identity from the call signalling and must be unique among all participants; a state attribute saying whether the information is full, partial or deleted; and child elements for display text, additional associated addresses of record, human-readable roles, the languages the user understands, and the cascaded-focus element holding the URI of a conference the user joined through focus cascading.

Endpoints are the devices and signalling sessions of a participant. An endpoint element has an entity key generated by the server and unique in the user context, such as a contact URI, and its own state attribute. Its children include display text, information about the user whose action brought the endpoint into the conference, the status of the endpoint, the method by which it joined and information about that, the method by which it departed and information about that, the media streams established with the focus, and detailed call signalling information.

The status of an endpoint can be connected, disconnected, on-hold, muted-via-focus, pending, alerting, dialing-in, dialing-out or disconnecting. A connected endpoint is a participant and, depending on the media policies, can send and receive media. A disconnected endpoint is not a participant and has no active dialog with the focus. An on-hold endpoint has an active dialog but is neither hearing the conference mix nor being mixed into it, for instance while waiting for moderator approval. A muted-via-focus endpoint can hear the conference but its media is not being mixed in. Pending, alerting, dialing-in, dialing-out and disconnecting are transient states, and because they could generate a lot of traffic, implementations may report them only to some participants or not at all.

A media element describes one media stream established between the focus and the endpoint. It has an id attribute that is the key for the stream, a display text, the media type, which must be one of the values registered for media in SDP, a label that identifies the stream among all streams in the conference, the source identifier, which for RTP streams is the SSRC value the endpoint generated, and the status, one of sendrecv, sendonly, recvonly or inactive, from the participant's point of view.
sections.plainLanguage: Each participant is listed with the devices they joined from, and each device carries a status such as connected, on hold or muted. The media streams in use are listed too, with the type of media and the identifier that identifies the source of each stream.

sections.title: An Example Document
sections.content:
The RFC's basic example is a full conference information document. The root element carries the namespace, the entity attribute holding the conference URI, state="full" and version="1". Inside it, the conference-description element carries a subject and a service-uris entry pointing at a web page, and the conference-state element carries a user count of 33.

The users element then holds a user element for each participant, keyed by the entity attribute. The first user is Bob Hoskins, whose endpoint is his laptop and whose status is disconnected, with a disconnection-method of departed and disconnection information giving the time, a reason of bad voice quality and the person who caused it. The endpoint also carries a media element with the id 1, display text 'main audio', type audio, label 34567, a source identifier of 432424 and status sendrecv. The second user is Alice, whose endpoint is connected, joined by dialed-out at the same time and by the same person, with its own media element carrying the label 34567 and a source identifier of 534232.
sections.plainLanguage: The worked example shows the shape of a document: the conference's own details, then one entry per participant with the devices they are on and the media they are sending.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Subscriptions to conference state information can reveal very sensitive information, so the RFC recommends that a focus use a strong means for authentication and for protecting the conference information, and that it apply comprehensive authorization rules when using the notification mechanism.

It is recommended that a focus authenticate a conference package subscriber using the normal SIP authentication mechanisms, such as Digest. The mechanism used to convey the conference information must ensure integrity and should ensure confidentiality, and an end-to-end SIP encryption mechanism such as S/MIME should be used to achieve that. If a strong end-to-end security means is not available, it is recommended that the focus use mutual hop-by-hop TLS authentication and encryption.

On authorization, a notification server must be capable of generating distinct conference information views for different subscribers, subject to a subscriber's role in the conference and personal access rights, and to local authorization policies. Because a focus provides participant identity information through this event package, participant privacy has to be taken into account: a focus must support requests by participants for privacy, whether indicated by the conference policy or in the session signalling, such as with the SIP Privacy header field. For a participant requesting privacy, no identity information should be revealed by the focus in any included URI, and the anonymous URI generation method in the document must be followed.
sections.plainLanguage: Conference state says who is on the call, so it is private information. Subscribers should be authenticated, the documents should be encrypted end to end, and a participant who asks not to be named should be shown with an anonymous address instead of their real one.

sections.title: Registry Assignments
sections.content: The RFC registers a SIP event package, a new MIME type, application/conference-info+xml, a new XML namespace and a new XML schema, and it creates a sub-registry for URI purposes under the existing SIP parameters registry. The conference event package is registered under the procedures of RFC 3265, with the package name conference.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC asks IANA to record the package name, the document format, the namespace and the schema, so that other specifications can refer to them by number.

viz.caption: The shape of a conference information document

children.label: user
children.note: Keyed by entity; contains endpoint elements, each with media elements

messages.label: SUBSCRIBE
messages.note: Subscribe to the conference package for the conference URI.

messages.label: NOTIFY (full state)
messages.note: The answer to the subscription carries the whole conference state.

messages.label: NOTIFY (partial state)
messages.note: Later notifications carry only what changed.

viz.caption: The states an endpoint can be in

items.label: CONNECTED
items.desc: The endpoint is a participant in the conference.

items.label: DISCONNECTED
items.desc: The endpoint is not a participant and has no active dialog with the focus.

items.label: ON-HOLD
items.desc: An active dialog exists, but the endpoint neither hears the mix nor is mixed in.

items.label: MUTED
items.desc: The endpoint can hear the conference but its media is not mixed in.

items.label: PENDING
items.desc: The endpoint is not yet in the session but is expected to join.

items.label: DIALING-IN
items.desc: The endpoint is dialing into the conference and is not yet in the roster.

items.label: DIALING-OUT
items.desc: The focus has dialed out to the endpoint, which is not yet in the roster.

items.label: DISCONNECTING
items.desc: The focus is in the process of disconnecting the endpoint.

viz.caption: What the state attribute can say

items.title: full
items.text: The element carries the whole of its information. This is the default.

items.title: partial
items.text: The element carries only what has changed since the last document.

items.title: deleted
items.text: The element has been removed from the conference state.

items.title: Consistency
items.text: A child of a full parent must be full; a child of a partial parent may be partial, full or deleted.

viz.caption: From the basic example in Section 7.1

data.title: conference-info
data.code:
<conference-info
 xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:conference-info"
 entity="sips:conf233@example.com"
 state="full" version="1">
 <conference-description>
  <subject>Agenda: This month's goals</subject>
 </conference-description>
 <conference-state>
  <user-count>33</user-count>
 </conference-state>
 <users>
  <user entity="sip:bob@example.com" state="full">
   <display-text>Bob Hoskins</display-text>
  </user>
 </users>
</conference-info>
